# opalstack_address (Resource)

A mail address. Mail sent to it is delivered to mailboxes, forwarded to other addresses, or both. The API accepts an address with neither, which accepts mail and keeps none of it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opalstack_address" "info" {
  source       = "info@${opalstack_domain.example.name}"
  mailuser_ids = [opalstack_mailuser.info.id]
  forwards     = ["someone@example.org"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `source` (String) The address itself, such as `info@example.com`. Its domain must be a domain of the account. Changing it replaces the address.

### Optional

- `forwards` (Set of String) Addresses the mail is sent on to. Left out, the list is empty on a new object and is left as it is on an existing one.
- `mailuser_ids` (Set of String) UUIDs of the mailboxes the mail is delivered to. Left out, the list is empty on a new object and is left as it is on an existing one.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the address.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the address itself, or by UUID.
terraform import opalstack_address.info info@example.com
terraform import opalstack_address.info 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
